concerns.text: FR-006 mandates packaging the pipeline in a reproducible Docker container, but no task in Phase 9–11 builds, documents, or verifies a Dockerfile (plan.md's Project Structure also has no Dockerfile entry). The dependency map claims 'FR-006 … T066, T073, T077 (foundation T006…)' but none of these tasks produces a container. Add a task that creates and smoke-tests the Dockerfile.

concerns.location: tasks.md:T073, T075, T076 vs constitution.md:Principle VII
concerns.text: Constitution VII requires effect sizes (AUC-ROC, precision-recall, R²) to be accompanied by 95% confidence intervals. No Phase 9–11 task computes CIs, and neither model_output.schema.yaml nor output.schema.yaml defines CI fields for effect sizes (only a single performance-level confidence_interval in output.schema). T073's verification validates against schemas that cannot carry the mandated CIs — a silent constitutional relaxation.

FR-009's train/hold-out ratios remain [deferred] in spec.md and plan.md, yet T073 commits to a concrete '--train-ratio default 0.8'. The implemented split is untraceable to any spec decision; resolve the [deferred] value in spec.md (or plan.md) so the task does not silently fix an open requirement.

T066 introduces halt code EX_RESOURCE_LIMIT (04), which appears in no functional requirement in spec.md and no plan-level decision record. Either add an FR authorizing it or record the plan decision; otherwise the task invents a requirement-level behavior.

T072 permits skipping fastp/bcftools variant calling when an accession provides pre-called variants ('direct VCF→dosage matrix via bcftools query'), narrowing FR-002's mandated preprocessing path with no spec/plan amendment recording the justification. Document the staged exception in spec.md or plan.md.

FR-007 and FR-008 assign two different halt codes (02 and 03) to substantively the same condition (<100 paired samples); T069/T072 inherit the contradiction. The spec should state which code fires or under which distinct conditions each applies, so task verification is unambiguous.

T073 requires outputs to validate against both model_output.schema.yaml and output.schema.yaml, but the schemas use conflicting field names for the same quantities (cv_score/null_baseline_score vs cv_accuracy/baseline_accuracy). A task could satisfy one and fail the other; reconcile the schemas or specify which output file targets which schema.
